translationRepairs: We have deliberated and ask to carry out the imperial will by assigning Attending Censor Zhang Chi, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Ju Keyou, Palace Attending Censor Shuai Ting, Director Deng Shouzhong of the Bureau of Appointments, Director Wang Ying of the Bureau of Granaries, Vice Director Jia Bi of the Bureau of Seals, Erudite Zhao Li of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Erudite Li Guangzan of the Directorate of Education, Senior Rectifier Su Xiao, Junior Mentor Wang Shen, and nine others—ten men in all—to compile new regulations and bind them into fascicles.

We have deliberated and ask to carry out the imperial will by assigning Attending Censor Zhang Chi, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Ju Keyou, Palace Attending Censor Shuai Ting, Director Deng Shouzhong of the Bureau of Appointments, Director Wang Ying of the Bureau of Granaries, Vice Director Jia Bi of the Bureau of Seals, Erudite Zhao Li of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Erudite Li Guangzan of the Directorate of Education, Senior Rectifier Su Xiao, Junior Mentor Wang Shen—ten men in all—to compile new regulations and bind them into fascicles.

Focus unit names exactly ten officials ending in 王伸等一十人; 等 closes the named list and 一十人 confirms the total is those ten. Adding 'and nine others' invents extra persons after all ten are already listed; the proposed cut restores the count.

Your subjects have deliberated and ask to carry out the sage edict, and further request that Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters Zhang Chi, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Ju Keyou, Palace Attending Censor Shuai Ting, Director of the Bureau of Appointments Deng Shouzhong, Director of the Bureau of Granaries Wang Ying, Vice Director of the Bureau of Seals Jia Bi, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhao Li, Erudite of the Directorate of Education Li Guangzan, Senior Rectifier Su Xiao, and Junior Mentor Wang Shen and nine others—ten men in all—be assigned to compile new regulations and bind them into fascicles.

Your subjects have deliberated and ask to carry out the sage edict, and further request that Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters Zhang Chi, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Ju Keyou, Palace Attending Censor Shuai Ting, Director of the Bureau of Appointments Deng Shouzhong, Director of the Bureau of Granaries Wang Ying, Vice Director of the Bureau of Seals Jia Bi, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhao Li, Erudite of the Directorate of Education Li Guangzan, Senior Rectifier Su Xiao, and Junior Mentor Wang Shen—ten men in all—be assigned to compile new regulations and bind them into fascicles.
The same Chinese list ends 王伸等一十人: ten named men, not ten including nine unnamed others. Removing 'and nine others' from the literal matches 一十人 without inventing surplus assignees.
We have examined the text and find the work throughout refined and thorough.
Your subjects Zhi and Pu have examined the text and find the work throughout refined and thorough.
Chinese opens with 臣質、臣溥 as the memorialists who 據文評議; the idiomatic 'We' drops those named subjects. Restoring Zhi and Pu recovers the attribution already present in the literal.
some are driven into false guilt;
Under 捶楚, 或陷無辜 means some innocent people are trapped or framed into guilt, not that anyone 'falls into guiltlessness.' The proposed wording matches that sense and the idiomatic field.

In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping, Emperor Taizu of Liang ordered Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Yan, Censor Xiao Qi, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Chong, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yi, Minister of Justice Wang Shan, and Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cui Gao to revise the statutes, ordinances, formats, and regulations together.

In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping, Emperor Taizu of Liang ordered Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Yan, Censor Xiao Qing, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Chong, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yi, Minister of Justice Wang Shan, and Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cui Gao to revise the statutes, ordinances, formats, and regulations together.
The censor is 蕭頃; 頃 is Qing (qǐng), not Qi. Replacing Xiao Qi with Xiao Qing corrects the given-name romanization while leaving titles and the rest of the sentence unchanged.

In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, an edict ordered Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Yan, Censor Xiao Qi, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Chong, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yi, Minister of Justice Wang Shan, and Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cui Gao jointly to revise the statutes, ordinances, formats, and regulations.

In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, an edict ordered Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Yan, Censor Xiao Qing, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Chong, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yi, Minister of Justice Wang Shan, and Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cui Gao jointly to revise the statutes, ordinances, formats, and regulations.
Literal likewise misreads 蕭頃 as Xiao Qi; Xiao Qing is the matching romanization of 頃 and aligns with the idiomatic repair.
